issues.description: Method SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery has inconsistent parameter lists between the problem statement and the code examples/solution. The UML and textual description in problem_statement.md declare acceptSupplyDelivery(String, String, int, int) (supplierName, ingredientName, price, quantity). However, both the template/example call in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java and the reference implementation in src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java use a three-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity). This discrepancy will confuse students about the correct method signature to implement and may cause compilation or test failures if tests or scaffolding expect the other signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across the problem statement, template/example code, and reference solution. Two valid resolutions: (A) Update the code (template and solution) to the four-parameter signature: public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and update all example calls (e.g., in Main) and any tests to pass a supplierName argument (supplierName may be stored, logged, or ignored). OR (B) Update the problem statement and UML to specify the three-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and remove the supplier parameter from descriptions and the UML. Choose the option that matches the intended automated tests; apply the chosen change everywhere (problem text, UML, template calls, and solution code) so students see a single, unambiguous signature.
